To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ADSCs promote bone defect rehabilitation by skewing differentiation of resident macrophages to M2 macrophage polarization, which is a new mechanism for ADSCs to promote bone repair in vivo.
ADSCs can promote bone defect repair in vivo via regulating the balance between M1 and M2 macrophage differentiation and osteogenic differentiation of ADSCs.
ADSCs promote bone defect rehabilitation by inducing BMDM polarization to M2 macrophage, which is a novel mechanism that has not been reported before.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of bone repair and the interaction of ADSCs and macrophages.
the interaction between ADSCs and BMDMs and their roles in the process of bone repair.
the interaction of ADSCs and BMDMs in bone tissue engineering, providing new insights into the mechanism of ADSCs mediated bone regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ADSCs are capable of promoting bone defect repair through M2 polarization of BMDMs.
ADSCs are capable of inducing M2 macrophage polarization in the host, which subsequently promotes osteogenic differentiation of the ADSCs, thus facilitating bone defect rehabilitation.
ADSCs can promote osteogenic differentiation of BMDMs and induce M2 polarization of macrophages, which in turn promote osteogenesis of ADSCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADSCs promote bone repair by inducing M2 macrophage polarization and osteogenic differentiation of ADSCs.
the ADSCs can be used as a cell therapy for bone regeneration in clinic.
the ADSCs and BMDM crosstalk can be exploited as a new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of bone damage and osteogenesis imperfecta, a genetic bone disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ADSCs are capable of inducing the polarization of BMDMs towards M2 macrophage, which in turn, can promote the differentiation of ADSCs to osteoblast, and thus contribute to the boney repair.
ADSCs may be a promising cell source in tissue repair.
the interaction between ADSCs and host cells may provide a potential strategy for the clinical application of ADSCs in the future.
